To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we observed the two astrophysically relevant resonant states at 4692 and 4813 keV in 32S(p, t)30S reaction, and we have determined their spectroscopic information, including the spin-parity assignments and the spectroscopic factors.

the 29P (p, γ) 30S reaction rate, which is important for understanding the nucleosynthesis in classical novae, has been determined using a new measurement of the 30S excited levels, including two states at 4692 keV and 4814 keV that are candidates to be the 3+ state and the previously missing 2+ state.
we have observed two states in 30Si that are candidates for being the two resonances that determine the 29P (p, γ) 30Si reaction rate at nova peak temperatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of astrophyscially important resonant states above the proton threshold in 30S, using the 32Si(p,t)30Si reaction.
the study of astrophysical resonant states in the 30S nucleus.
the determination of the astrophysically relevant 29P(p,gamma)30S reaction rates at nova temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have observed the two states that are important for the determination of the 29P(γ,p)30S reaction rates, but we have not been able to identify them conclusively.
we have observed all the 29P proton unbound states that are important for determining the 29P+p→30S reaction rate in novae.
we have observed two new states in 30Si at 4693 keV and 4814 keV that are candidates of the 3+ state and previously missing 2+ state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have observed all states that are important in the astrophysically relevant energy region.
the 29P proton capture reaction on 30P is now well understood, and the reaction rate is now well determined.
we have observed 14 levels in 30S and we are confident to assign the spin and parity of 3+ to the 4692.9 keV state and the 2+ to the 4813.9 keV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the previously “missing,” 2+ state is not a 2+ state at all, but a 4+ state, which is the second excited state above the 2+ ground state.
the 3+ state is located at 4692±4.5 keV and that the “missing” 29P(p,g)30S resonance at 4813.5 keVs has a 2+ spin‐parity.
we have observed two levels that can contribute to the 29P (p,γ)30 S reaction rate at nova temperature.
